prompt: Our government agency is building an AI system to automatically screen and determine eligibility for social welfare benefits — housing assistance, food support, unemployment. It will replace manual case workers for initial screening decisions. Run the full Stanford Ethics Toolkit chain (Future Story → Impacts Explorer → Ethics Frame → Ethics Gauge → Weighing Options) with the following two options: Option A is to deploy the AI as the primary decision-maker with a human appeals process; Option B is to use the AI as a decision-support tool only, with all final decisions made by case workers.
assertions: Output contains a Future Story section
Output contains an Impacts Explorer section
Output contains an Ethics Frame section
Output contains an Ethics Gauge section
Output contains a Weighing Options section
Option A (AI as primary decision-maker) is analyzed in the Weighing Options section
Option B (AI as decision-support with human final decisions) is analyzed in the Weighing Options section
At least three distinct stakeholder groups are named (e.g., applicants, case workers, agency, vulnerable populations)
Values of justice and dignity are explicitly named
A Future Direction or recommendation section appears that names which option to pursue and why
